name: Abū Dāwūd ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Hurmuz al-Aʿraj
summary: Qurʾān reader and transmitter of Medina, learned in Arabic and in the genealogies of the Arabs, whom al-Zubaydī counts with Abū al-Aswad in the first generation of the grammarians; he died in Alexandria in 117/735.
bio: Al-Aʿraj ('the lame') was a client of Muḥammad ibn Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, a reader of the Qurʾān and transmitter of ḥadīth, learned in Arabic and, in Ibn al-Anbārī's words, the most learned of men in the genealogies of the Arabs. He went to Alexandria and lived there until his death in 117/735, in the reign of Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik.
Al-Zubaydī names him in the first generation of the grammarians of Basra, beside Abū al-Aswad, and some reports make him one of the first to lay down Arabic grammar.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 18–19
Abdurrahman b. Hürmüz, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
